Drama game of the Week: Mirror, Mirror
By admin
9 Nov 2023
0 Comments
Hey everybody!
Can you believe that there are fewer than 60 days left until 2024? It’s time to finish what you start! But first: read our game of the week.
This week we will provide you again with a valuable resource for actors and acting enthusiasts looking to enhance their non-verbal communication abilities and establish stronger connections with their fellow performers.
In the drama game “Mirror, Mirror,” the primary objective is to enhance non-verbal communication and connect with your scene partner. Here are the basic rules and steps for playing this game:
Pairing Up: Find a partner to play the game with. This game works best with two actors, but you can adapt it for larger groups by forming pairs.
Select a Leader: In each pair, choose one actor to be the “leader” and the other to be the “mirror.”
Begin the Scene: The leader initiates a scene or scenario by performing a simple, non-verbal action or movement. This could be anything from pouring a cup of tea to playing catch.
Mirroring: The mirror’s task is to closely observe the leader and replicate their actions as accurately and in real time as possible. This includes mimicking their body language, gestures, facial expressions, and movements.
Communication: Without using any verbal communication, the leader should try to guide the mirror through the scene. The mirror should pay close attention to the leader’s non-verbal cues and respond accordingly.
Switch Roles: After a certain amount of time, or when you feel the scene has progressed sufficiently, switch roles. The mirror becomes the leader, and vice versa.
Debrief: After both actors have had a chance to lead and mirror, take a moment to discuss the experience. Talk about what worked well, any challenges you encountered, and what you learned about non-verbal communication and connecting with your scene partner.
“Mirror, Mirror” is a valuable exercise for building trust, improving observation skills, and fostering a deeper connection between actors. It’s a great way to enhance non-verbal communication, which is essential in theatrical performances. It’s a great addition to your movement classes and a true pillar of every drama school in the world.
